items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I knew Walter Paige before because when I was in Sioux City, Iowa, stationed there with Grant Moore, the Blue Devils were stationed there, too. They were playing in Sioux City and they had Lester Young and Buster Smith and Theodore Ross was playing lead alto.

ctx.x: So Macleo Burchell was his manager. We all drove on in his car, his Ford. And they had their bus, or whatever it is, and we went to Kansas City. And Benny revamped his band. I was put on lead alto with Ben Webster and Jack Washington. And we had Eddie Durham on banjo -- on guitar and trombone. And we had Dan Minor on trombone. And we had Hot Lips Paige. And at that time we had Joe Smith, Russell Smith's brother on trumpet and Hot Lips Paige and Joe Keyes. He was my roommate. And gee, Joe, he was playing first.…

Of course, I knew Walter Paige before because when I was in Sioux City, Iowa, stationed there with Grant Moore, the Blue Devils were stationed there, too. They were playing in Sioux City and they had Lester Young and Buster Smith and
Theodore Ross was playing lead alto. And Lester Young and all of them were there in Sioux City at that time.

items.title: 56711_Buster Smith oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Barefield, he was on alto, and Lester was on tenor... Eddie Barefield was in it.

ctx.x: We went to Minneapolis and played the dates/the bass(?) there, and we got through playing that night, and we went down where Lester was playing with Frank Hine and Eddie Barefield. It was about seven or eight pieces. So we went up there, and they played until I guess two or three or four o'clock in the morning. Anyway, we went up there and had dinner. Then they asked me to sit in with them and play somethin'. So I got in and played three or four numbers. So we...
Now, just a minute. Lester was playing alto then or tenor?
